entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Toma Niger was a Croatian humanist, diplomat, bishop of Skradin, and at the end of his life he served as the bishop of Trogir. Born in an unknown year, he dedicated most of his life to diplomacy, striving to help the crumbling Kingdom of Croatia against the Ottoman Empire.

Toma Niger's significance extends to his efforts as a diplomat, as he worked tirelessly to strengthen ties between Croatia and the Catholic Church.

As a bishop, he played a crucial role in the religious and cultural landscape of 16th-century Croatia.

Toma Niger's legacy is marked by his commitment to diplomacy and his efforts to preserve Croatian culture in the face of Ottoman expansion.

A testament to his dedication, Toma Niger was appointed as the bishop of Trogir in 1524, a position he held until his death in 1531.

In a time of great turmoil, Toma Niger's unwavering commitment to his faith and his people left an indelible mark on Croatian history.
